chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked about prayer on a ship, and he said: 'If you are able to go out to the Qibla (the deck/open area), then go out; and if you cannot, then pray standing; and if you cannot, then pray sitting, and seek the Qibla.'

key_terms.الْجَدَدِ: the deck or open area of the ship (specifically the part facing the Qibla)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for praying on a ship if one cannot go to the deck?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *takhfif* (easing) in prayer based on physical capability, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on practicality during travel. It highlights the hierarchy of postures—standing, then sitting—while maintaining the obligation of facing the Qibla as much as possible, a ruling derived from the flexibility granted in the Quranic verse of travel. This hadith serves as a primary textual basis for the Shia school's specific regulations regarding *Salat al-Musafir* when sea travel prevents standard prayer conditions.
